{{short description|Russian and American mathematician (1886-1944)}}
'''James Alexander Shohat''' ({{a.k.a.}} Jacques Chokhate (or Chokhatte) {{langx|ru|Яков Александрович Шохат}}, 18 November 1886, [[Brest, Belarus|Brest-Litovsk]] – 8 October 1944, [[Philadelphia]]) was a Russian and American mathematician at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] who worked on the [[moment problem]].<ref name="obit">{{cite journal|author=Kline, J. R.|authorlink=John Robert Kline|title=Obituary: James Alexander Shohat|journal=Science|date=3 November 1944 |volume=100|issue=2601|pages=397–398|doi=10.1126/science.100.2601.397|pmid=17799450}}</ref> He studied at the [[University of Petrograd]] and married the physicist [[Nadiashda Galli-Shohat|Nadiascha W. Galli]], the couple emigrating from Russia to the United States in 1923.<ref name="obit"/> 

He was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in 1924 at Toronto.<ref>Shohat, J. A. [http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1924.1/Main/icm1924.1.0611.0618.ocr.pdf "On the asymptotic properties of a certain class of Tchebycheff polynomials."] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201041559/http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1924.1/Main/icm1924.1.0611.0618.ocr.pdf |date=2017-12-01 }} In Proc. Intern. Math. Congress Toronto, pp. 611–618. 1924.</ref>

==Selected works==
* {{cite journal|title=On a general formula in the theory of Tchebycheff polynomials and its applications|journal=Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.|year=1927|volume=29|issue=3|pages=569–583|mr=1501405|doi=10.1090/s0002-9947-1927-1501405-8|doi-access=free|last1=Shohat|first1=J.}}
* {{cite journal|title=A simple method for normalizing Tchebycheff polynomials and evaluating the elements of the allied continued fractions|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|year=1927|volume=33|issue=4|pages=427–432|mr=1561395|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1927-04396-8|doi-access=free|last1=Shohat|first1=J. A.}}
* with J. Sherman: {{cite journal|title=On the numerators of the continued fraction|journal=Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A|year=1932|volume=18|issue=3|pages=283–287|pmc=1076208|doi=10.1073/pnas.18.3.283|pmid=16587678|doi-access=free|last1=Shohat|first1=J.|last2=Sherman|first2=J.}}
* {{cite journal|title=On the development of functions in a series of polynomials|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|year=1935|volume=41|issue=2|pages=49–82|mr=1563024|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1935-06007-0|doi-access=free}}
* {{cite journal|title=Mechanical quadratures, in particular, with positive coefficients|journal=Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.|year=1937|volume=42|issue=3|pages=461–496|mr=1501930|doi=10.1090/s0002-9947-1937-1501930-6|doi-access=free|last1=Shohat|first1=J.}}<ref>18 Aug. 2012 email from [[Richard Askey|R. Askey]]: "I suspect that "On mechanical quadratures, in particular, with positive coefficients", Trans AMS 42 (1937), 461-496 is the most important paper among those dealing with interpolation and quadrature, but I am not an expert on this and have not read enough to be sure."</ref>
* {{cite journal|title=A differential equation for orthogonal polynomials|journal=Duke Math. J.|year=1939|volume=5|issue=2|pages=401–417|mr=1546133|doi=10.1215/s0012-7094-39-00534-x|last1=Shohat|first1=J.}}<ref>18 Aug. 2012 email from R. Askey: 
"I am not an expert on all of Shohat's work, but I think the most important paper is: A differential equation for orthogonal polynomials, Duke
Math Journal, 5(1939)401-417.  In it he finds a difference equation for a coefficient in the recurrence relation for polynomials orthogonal on the real line with respect to e^(-x^4).  It turns out that this nonlinear difference equation is a discrete analogue of one of the [[Painlevé transcendents|Painleve differential equations]], and I think the first discrete Painleve equation found."</ref>
* with [[Jacob Tamarkin|J. D. Tamarkin]]: {{cite book|title=The problem of moments|series=Mathematical Surveys, vol. 1|year=1943|location=New York|publisher=AMS|oclc=622772715}}<ref>{{cite journal|author=Widder, D. V.|authorlink=David Widder|title=Review: J. A. Shohat and J. D. Tamarkin, ''The problem of moments''|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|year=1945|volume=51|issue=11|pages=860–863|url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.bams/1183507424|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1945-08459-6|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* {{cite journal|title=On van der Pol's and non-linear differential equations|journal=J. Appl. Phys.|year=1944|volume=15|issue=7|pages=568–574|doi=10.1063/1.1707470}}<ref>18 Aug. 2012 email from R. Askey: "[[Norman Levinson]] give the following paper a very strong review. On van der Pol's and non-linear differential equations, J. Appl. Phys15 (1944), 568-574 [along with giving a very strong negative comment on Shohat's earlier paper on von der Pol's equation]."</ref>
